obernants.observation_scope: Typed errors, canonical graph/code outputs and named assertions
obernants.operator: U is all (n,ordered signed edges,candidate Result) triples. On valid graphs, outputs containing loops, cycles, a nonspanning partition, wrong total, or greater-than-minimum weight are excluded; alternative equal-weight forests are also excluded if their index list differs from deterministic rounds. On invalid inputs, Ok is excluded; the first typed validation error is fixed.

obernants.operator: Fix observed F. The fiber includes every ordered multigraph whose deterministic rounds select those indices, whose selected weights sum to F.total_weight, and whose connectivity gives F.components. Unselected heavier edges, loops, and redistributed selected weights may be invisible. Even fixing n and selected indices does not reconstruct edge endpoints or all weights.

obernants.operator: Holding endpoints and weights fixed, reindexing equal-weight edges may change the chosen index forest. In a two-vertex parallel pair with equal weights the first input edge wins; endpoint direction is immaterial. Ordering is an API contract, not uniqueness of the unconstrained minimum forest.

obernants.operator: Fix an ordered edge list and n. If n>1000000, TooManyVertices wins even if edge count or labels are invalid. Otherwise E>4000000 gives TooManyEdges before inspecting endpoints. Otherwise the first invalid endpoint in edge-index order, u before v, determines InvalidEndpoint; a self-loop outside 0..n is rejected rather than silently ignored. Errors therefore identify a prefix boundary and do not reconstruct later edges. Witnesses boundary_and_validation cover caps and invalid endpoints; simultaneous-invalid precedence is source-derived, not separately exhaustively tested.

obernants.operator: Fix n and the full returned (sorted edge_indices,total_weight,components). The selected indices identify original input occurrences, not normalized endpoint pairs; reversing endpoints leaves their identity intact. Projecting further to only (total_weight,components) loses both selected indices and tree shape. For n=3 the unit-weight paths [(0,1),(1,2)] and [(0,2),(1,2)] both yield weight 2 and one component despite different trees. signed_wide_total_and_ties separately constrains index identity [0,1], count 2 and signed sum, so matching only scalar cost is insufficient.
